description:
Run virtual services in your network

You use VirtServer to run virtual services in your network. It is an addition to ReadyAPI Virtualization that is used for creating, editing, and running virtualized services.
VirtServer is tightly integrated with ReadyAPI Virtualization, allowing you to run and manage virtual services created with ReadyAPI Virtualization and hosted on VirtServer. VirtServer runs on Windows, Linux, macOS, and headless machines .
- VirtServer 3.35.1 is a patch release.
- Security Mitigation for CVE-2026-114938
  A high-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938, CVSS 3.1 score 8.1) affects the OpenJDK Compiler component. The Java runtime in VirtServer relies on this component. On x86-64 systems with AVX-512 VBMI, the vulnerability allows remote code execution through memory corruption. Attackers can exploit it only by supplying data to affected APIs, for example, through a web service.
  VirtServer 3.35.1 includes the JVM flags that mitigate the vulnerability. Upgrade to VirtServer 3.35.1 to apply the mitigation. VirtServer 3.36.0 will update the bundled OpenJDK version to fix the vulnerability.
- Workaround for Earlier Versions
  If you cannot upgrade yet, add one of the following flags to the JVM startup parameters:
  - Disable Base64 intrinsics (recommended): -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics
  - Disable AVX-512 execution (x86-64 only): -XX:UseAVX=2
  Both flags can affect application performance. Test them in your environment before a wide rollout.
  To apply the flag, add it to the JVM options file for VirtServer, then restart the application:
  - VirtServer: VirtServer.vmoptions or VirtServer-service.vmoptions
  - Docker: Set the JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS environment variable, for example, -e JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS="-XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics".
  For help, contact SmartBear Support.
